articles.title: Rainwater enters Gujarat University mess - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Ahmedabad: Heavy rainfall has triggered severe waterlogging across the
Gujarat University (GU) campus, leaving students at the Samaras hostels struggling to cope with flooded premises.
The Samaras boys’ and girls’ hostels on the campus were among the worst affected as continuous rain led to knee-deep water accumulation in several parts of the area. Rainwater entered the hostel premises and flooded the mess, forcing students to have their meals while standing in water.
Students said they had to wade through water to move in and out of the hostels, while many remained confined indoors due to the flooding.
According to students, waterlogging during the monsoon has been a recurring problem for several years.
Similar scenes were reported from other parts of the campus, including areas near the Atal-Kalam Research Park where large stretches resembled waterbodies due to accumulated rainwater.
Students have questioned the effectiveness of the campus drainage system, alleging that despite substantial spending on infrastructure and renovation projects, basic issues such as rainwater disposal remain unresolved.
NSUI activists have also demanded immediate intervention by university authorities to address the problem and prevent its recurrence during future monsoons.

articles.title: Traffic disrupted on over 1,100 roads across Gujarat; 365 stretches reopened - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Gandhinagar: Heavy rainfall across Gujarat has disrupted traffic on 1,109 roads, including national highways, state highways, panchayat roads, and other key routes.
According to the State Emergency Operations Centre, traffic movement has been affected on eight stretches of national highways, 34 state highways, 38 other roads and 1,029 panchayat roads. Waterlogging, fallen trees and rain-related damage have led to the closures.
The Sanand-Viramgam stretch of the Ahmedabad-Viramgam highway has been closed to traffic. Movement has also been affected on the Bavla-Sarkhej, Kheda-Dholka and Matar-Tarapur highways, besides several state highway stretches in Valsad, Navsari and Dang districts due to heavy waterlogging.
The state govt said restoration work is underway on all closed roads. So far, traffic has been restored on 365 roads, with around 1,500 personnel, 225 JCB machines and more than 1,500 other machines deployed to clear debris and reopen road links.

articles.title: Receding waters uncover flood devastation, 31 dead in Gujarat - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Receding waters uncover flood devastation, 31 dead in Gujarat
After battering south Gujarat and Ahmedabad, the southwest monsoon fury turned to north Gujarat and parts of Saurashtra on Friday.
Even as downpours stopped in south Gujarat, the flood situation remained grim as helicopters continued multiple sorties to airlift stranded residents, and rescue teams worked overtime to evacuate people from inundated areas.
Mehemdabad in Kheda district was pounded by 507 mm in 24 hours ending 6 am Friday, the highest in the state. Between 6 am and 8 pm on Friday, Santalpur in Patan recorded the highest rainfall of 335 mm.
Relief commissioner Gaurang Makwana said 38,000 people have been relocated so far, primarily from the Navsari and Valsad districts. “Most of these people have shifted to their relatives’ homes, while about 2,000 have been moved to shelter homes. A total of 352 people have been rescued so far.”
In Navsari, an Indian Coast Guard helicopter airlifted 60 shrimp farm workers stranded in Mendhar village, while an Indian Army column was deployed alongside NDRF and SDRF teams to assist in rescue efforts. Rail services remained disrupted, with more than 50 trains cancelled and 25 short-terminated.
The gradually receding waters exposed a trail of devastation — bridges, roads and neighbourhoods were buried under thick layers of sludge, plastic waste, uprooted vegetation and debris.
Four NDRF teams, airlifted from Odisha, landed in Surat and were dispatched to Valsad and Navsari, and one was kept on standby in Surat. Two Army columns reached Valsad and Navsari, and two additional teams were dispatched in the affected districts.

articles.title: Gujarat CM visits waterlogged Bopal, Ghuma, Ambli, interacts with affected people - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Gujarat CM visits waterlogged Bopal, Ghuma, Ambli, interacts with affected people
An official statement said Patel asked officials to speed up relief and rescue operations and arrange the manpower, equipment and other support needed.
The chief minister then met officials, including the city police commissioner, municipal commissioner, state relief commissioner and mayor, at the AMC’s north-west zone office.
Sources said the CM directed the administration to take immediate steps to clear the affected areas and restore normalcy soon.
Rushikesh Patel, minister in charge of Ahmedabad, directed AMC officials to clear the waterlogging at the earliest. “Waterlogging has taken much longer to recede in parts of western Ahmedabad. Pumps have been pressed into service, and we expect the water to recede in all areas by 6pm today (Friday),” he said.
The minister said the state govt had been working with the AMC on stormwater drainage projects, and that the western trunk line project — already sanctioned — would help contain waterlogging in most parts of Ahmedabad.

articles.title: GCCI launches flood relief drive, prepares 6,000 food packets - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Ahmedabad: The Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI) has launched a flood relief drive and prepared 6,000 food packets for people affected by heavy rain and waterlogging across Ahmedabad.
The chamber has set up a help desk and partnered with its member organisations, the Robin Hood Army and other voluntary groups to identify and reach affected families in rain-hit areas.
Each food packet contains teekhi poori, bataka sabji, and sukhdi. GCCI said the relief campaign will continue for the next two to three days, with more food packets to be prepared depending on demand and the situation across the city.
“We are working to ensure that families affected by flooding receive timely food assistance. We will continue the relief drive for the next few days and scale up support wherever required,” said Sandeep Engineer, president, GCCI.
